akhenaten-card.jpg.note: At the altar in the open court of the Great Temple of the Aten at Akhetaten, about 1345 BC. THE GUARD FAILED ON EVERY COUNT AND IT IS THE ONE GUARD THAT INVERTED. Every other figure in this deck carries 'no likeness survives, render a characteristic face rather than a portrait'; Akhenaten has hundreds of surviving portraits and the instruction was DO NOT NORMALISE HIM. The plate returned a conventional pharaoh: six-pack abdominals, broad square shoulders, flat stomach, muscular chest, an ordinary skull and jaw. None of the Amarna features survived - no elongated skull, no drooping jaw, no soft chest, no swollen belly, no wide hips. The ray-hands are also gone: the disc carries plain radiating spokes rather than rays ending in small human hands holding ankhs, which is the single detail that identifies which pharaoh this is. The altar additionally blocks the figure from the waist down. WHY THE GUARD LOST: it sat at the END of a long passage that had already specified crown, collar, linen, gold and sandals, so the model had built a king before the deformity clauses arrived. A re-roll should lead with the body. MEASURED WORST IN THE DECK: value_span 148.3 is the FIRST PLATE EVER TO FAIL THAT ENFORCED RULE (floor 170); radial key 0.031 is the flattest measured; 1.2% of frame under 40/255 against a previous minimum of 5%; mean luminance 153, the brightest plate in the deck. Span and key cannot be corrected by CSS grading the way saturation can. Kept as it stands by choice.

albert-einstein-card.jpg.note: Outside the Swiss Federal Office for Intellectual Property at night, Bern, 1905 - technical expert third class, twenty-six years old, patent files under one arm and his own scruffier sheaf in his hands. Wet arcade, gas lamp, tram-lit street beyond. THE AGE GUARD HELD, WHICH WAS THE WHOLE RISK: thick dark brown hair neatly combed, full dark moustache, a young unlined face. NO white halo, no cardigan, no pipe, no tongue out - the famous likeness is fifty years later and it is the only Einstein the model knows, so the guard states the age as a flat refusal rather than a description. That is the Gandhi lesson: six polite requests for small round wire spectacles failed where 'he is fat' landed first roll. 40% of frame under 40/255, the deepest shadow of any card in the deck, span 226.3, nothing blown. NO ROOM: there is no library/albert-einstein.json. A figure can carry plates and a quiz without one, so this is a state rather than a fault. FILENAME: the ledger's Full Name cell reads 'Albert Einstein', which the CSV loader slugs to albert-einstein - confirmed before ingest, because that is exactly how Musashi's plates were built as miyamoto-musashi-* when the roster said musashi.

charles-darwin-card.jpg.note: The Galapagos shore, 1835, aged twenty-six - crouched on black lava with a live mocking-thrush standing on the rim of a vessel at his elbow, a dead specimen on the rock in front, an open field notebook weighted with a pebble, pencil, specimen bag, the hammer handle at the edge of frame. Prickly-pear cactus behind him, the sea beyond. STRONGEST ROSTER LEGIBILITY OF ANY CARD: tile_contrast 92.1, measured at the 198x160 thumbnail size, the highest in the deck. Span 225.0, radial key 0.445 from the left as specified, 45.9% under 40/255, nothing blown. THE PRIOR IS DATED FROM THE ROOM, which is the practice that landed plates first-roll all session: library/charles-darwin.json opens with the Galapagos passage about how unafraid the birds are, in which a mocking-thrush lands on the rim of a tortoise-shell pitcher he is holding and drinks from it. The live bird and the dead specimen are in the same frame because he was collecting and observing in the same motion, and that is the method entire. THE AGE GUARD HELD, THIRD TIME THIS SESSION AND THE HARDEST CASE: clean-shaven, thick reddish-brown hair, side-whiskers, a young open face. The white-bearded patriarch is the ONLY Darwin anyone pictures and that beard does not arrive until the 1860s, thirty years after the Beagle. Einstein at 26 not 76 and Dickens at 31 not 60 were the same guard. Age is arithmetic: born 1809, Galapagos 1835. CHOSEN OVER AN ALTERNATE ROLL that measured radial key 0.529, the strongest ever recorded here, and 56.2% shadow. This one was taken instead because the bird reads unmistakably as a Galapagos mocking-thrush - long decurved bill, streaked breast - where the alternate's read as a generic thrush, and because tile_contrast is higher on the surface that matters. TWO DEFECTS ACCEPTED: accent 0.373, high for a card; and 816x1456, sub-spec, UPSAMPLED to 1120. MIDJOURNEY v7.

charles-darwin-terminal.jpg.note: The desk at night, 1844, aged thirty-five - the fourteen years of silence. DEEPEST SHADOW IN THE DECK at 82.5% of frame under 40/255, taking that record from charles-dickens-terminal at 74.2%. Span 231.3, radial key 0.330 from the right as specified. HE IS NOT WRITING, AND THAT IS THE BRIEF: one hand flat on the finished manuscript bundle tied with tape, the other beside a sheet, barnacle specimens on the desk in front of him. In 1844 he enlarged the pencil sketch to 230 pages, had it fair-copied, and left instructions and money for his wife to publish it if he died - then said nothing for fourteen more years, and buried himself in barnacles for eight of them. Shelves of specimen boxes going up into blackness, candles burned low, the fireplace cold. The age guard held again: clean-shaven, reddish-brown hair receding at the temples, side-whiskers, a drawn tired face. THREE DEFECTS ACCEPTED: accent 0.427, the candles warm across a wide area, so the CSS grade pulls it hard; tile_contrast 45.2, low, which would matter on a card but not on an absorbed plate behind text; and 816x1456, sub-spec, UPSAMPLED to 1120. charles-dickens-card.jpg.note: A London street at night, 1843, aged thirty-one - stopped mid-stride on wet cobbles under a gas lamp, half-turned, looking at something off to one side. He walked fifteen and twenty miles a night through the city and took everything down; the figure half-seen in the fog down the street is what the walking was for. THE AGE GUARD HELD, WHICH WAS THE WHOLE RISK: clean-shaven, thick dark hair long to the collar, a young sharp face. The bearded patriarch everyone pictures is 1858 onward, fifteen years later, and it is the only Dickens the model knows. Figured waistcoat, cravat, rings, cane - he was a dandy and was mocked for it. BEST LIGHTING IN THE DECK: span 235.3, 59% of frame under 40/255 which is the second deepest of any card, radial key 0.323 from the left as specified, almost nothing blown. FIRST MIDJOURNEY PLATE IN THE DECK. The FLUX prompts do not transfer - Midjourney weights early tokens and drops detail past roughly 60-80 words, and it largely ignores negation and can summon what you name, so the guards moved out of the prose and into --no. See PROMPT_charles-dickens_MIDJOURNEY.txt. THREE DEFECTS ACCEPTED: it is TRUE MONOCHROME with a warm sepia cast rather than the deck's near-monochrome with one warm accent on metal, so accent 0.347 measures the cast and not a colour accent - with more Midjourney plates this becomes a visible split in the deck; generated at 816x1456, sub-spec, so UPSAMPLED to 1120 where the standard is 2048 downsampled; and the figure sits further from camera than the card brief asked, though it reads at thumbnail size. CROPPED BEFORE INGEST: 28px taken off the TOP rather than the bottom, at the proprietor's direction, to keep the ground and bring the ratio to exactly 0.571 - ingest only ever trims from the bottom, so a tighter frame has to be taken off the top before it.

charles-dickens-terminal.jpg.note: The desk at Devonshire Terrace, autumn 1843, writing A Christmas Carol. He read the Second Report on child labour, planned a pamphlet called An Appeal to the People of England on behalf of the Poor Man's Child, abandoned it, and wrote this instead in six weeks - telling Dr Southwood Smith a story would come down with twenty thousand times the force. DEEPEST SHADOW IN THE DECK: 74.2% of frame under 40/255, taking that record from isaac-newton-terminal at 70.5%. Span 237.0, radial key 0.289 from the right as specified, nothing blown. Thirty-one and clean-shaven, hair long to the collar - the age guard held again. Hunched close, writing fast with a goose quill, manuscript sheets spilling off the desk edge onto the floor, shelved books going up into blackness, shuttered window, fire burned low in the grate, a brass oil lamp as the only real source. THE TWO BRONZE DESK ORNAMENTS ARE PRESENT - the duelling toads and the dog-fancier with puppies, which he carried everywhere and could not write without - and so is the geranium and the bottle of blue ink. MIDJOURNEY, like the card. See PROMPT_charles-dickens_MIDJOURNEY.txt for why the FLUX prompts do not transfer. The moon, the farmhouse with its lit window, the drystone wall and the old orchard all landed. SECOND ROLL. The first was the night version as briefed and measured tile_contrast 29.7 with mean luminance 37 - the darkest plate in the deck and by a wide margin the least legible at the 198x160 roster thumbnail, where it read as a smudge. seneca-card.jpg.note: The bath, AD 65, ordered to die by his own pupil. THE GUARD LANDED ON THE BODY: gaunt, sinewy, hollow-cheeked, thin grey hair, clean-shaven, an old man's frame - Tacitus records that an austere diet had wasted him. The secretary standing behind, still writing, is the detail that carries the plate: he went on dictating throughout. THREE DEVIATIONS ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY. The tub returned ROUND where the brief specified a long rectangle. The blood is a vivid red ribbon on the surface rather than the faint clouding thread written - still no wound in frame, no red bath, nothing graphic, but more emphatic than briefed. And the face reads slightly strained where the entire brief was composure. Also note this is a LIGHT plate: 5% of frame under 40/255, mean luminance 117, span 181 - second lightest in the deck. ON THE DEATH BEING THE CARD: this is his roster face, chosen deliberately because it is the one thing everyone knows about him and what the argument finally cost.

shaka-card.jpg.note: Before his regiments in dawn mist at kwaBulawayo, about 1824. STRONGEST KEY IN THE DECK at radial 0.491, taking the record from hannibal-card at 0.433. THE SHIELD GUARD WORKED ON THE SECOND ROLL: the first returned a small round disc, and rewriting the clause by SIZE AGAINST A BODY PART - a full cowhide from chin to knee, oval, NOT round and NOT small - produced the correct isihlangu, and the ranks behind him carry the same, so the shield wall reads. That is the Gandhi lesson applied: six polite requests for small round wire spectacles failed where he is fat landed first roll. Describe the thing, then refuse the default. TWO DEFECTS ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY. FIRST, the spear is still LONG-HAFTED and held vertically like a staff: the blade came back broad and leaf-shaped, so half the clause landed, but no longer than a forearm, gripped underhand at the hip did not. The iklwa is the single thing he is most remembered for. SECOND, the specified sunrise never arrived - flat grey mist, no god-rays, no raking light - which is why true shadow is 12.5% against the first roll's 24.8% and mean luminance rose to 112.6. THE ROOM: he left no writing, so library/shaka.json holds two archives and labels which is which - three izibongo as plain-English renderings of the praise-names, and three travellers' accounts still to be sourced from Isaacs 1836 and Bryant 1929.

tacitus-terminal.jpg.note: About AD 116, twenty years on, writing the Annals alone by a two-wick bronze lamp. Pigeonholed scroll shelving behind, lamp smoke rising through the key, and a MARBLE BUST OF TIBERIUS on a plinth at the edge of the light, facing him - the emperor whose reign he is writing, watching him work. Toga removed and every highlight moved onto bronze, lamp oil and marble, which is why this plate holds its speculars where a wool-heavy one would not. ONE DEFECT ACCEPTED: he writes with a bronze stylus on parchment rather than cutting into wax - a stylus is a wax instrument.
